description: S328 merge-blocker — the §4.14 byte-identity contract stated as a runtime case, for the ONE content model where the two branches could disagree. The same body is written FOUR ways inside an RCDATA parent (<textarea>): `:`-shorthand and bare-body, each with a mixed-return fn CALL and with a plain member expression. All four must agree on DOM SHAPE — no element child in any of them. This is the case that fails if a future change fixes one branch's RCDATA handling and not the other's.
rationale: SPEC §4.14 line 1021: 'a `:`-shorthand body IS the element's single-expression body, byte-identical to the bare-body form `<tag>${expr}</tag>`'; §17.7.6 lines 12176-12177 carry it into <each> scope with no <each>-specific extension. Both emit-each branches read ONE local (`_isRcdataBody`) so they cannot drift. NOTE, deliberately narrow: this pins the two `<each>` per-item branches and NOTHING ELSE. Three other answers to 'may this body receive an element child?' exist and are not routed through that local — `eachRcdataValueExpr`'s null-bail falls through to the mounting recursion inside the same file, `emit-html.ts` runs its own `isRcdataElement` check for the top-level path, and the Tier-0 `lift` path answers separately again. An earlier revision of this case asserted a whole-document `[data-scrml-mv]` count of 0; that was overstated and is gone — <option> mounts legitimately (see each-shorthand-option-label-preserved).
